description: Tier-1 self-authored Figma fixtures for the dashscene importer (see docs/decisions/figma-corpus-self-authored-only.md). Each entry maps a fixture name to the Figma file key of a file authored in the project's own account. The capture tooling fetches GET /files/:fileKey?plugin_data=shared (docs/decisions/figma-access-plan-and-pat-policy.md, docs/decisions/annotator-plugin-contract-frozen.md) and commits the returned JSON into corpus/figma-fixtures/<name>.json for offline record-and-replay (docs/design/dashc.md).
provenance: self-authored via the fixture-author dev plugin (importers/figma/plugins/fixture-author); Community-license-safe because nothing captured here is a third-party file (docs/decisions/figma-corpus-self-authored-only.md).

captureParams.note: ?plugin_data=shared is always passed so sharedPluginData roles (docs/decisions/annotator-plugin-contract-frozen.md) round-trip even though no fixture carries them yet.

fixtures.name: grid-basic
fixtures.covers: GRID mode: row/column spans, fixed+flex tracks, hug/fill/fixed children, min/max constraints
fixtures.note: Lowers since #264 (the v0.8 grid un-pin): GRID -> LayoutMode::Grid with gridColumnGap/gridRowGap as the main/cross gaps, the gridColumnsSizing/gridRowsSizing strings as Fixed/Fraction track lists, and per-child anchors/spans as placement (docs/decisions/figma-flex-lowering.md D5, docs/decisions/v08-layout-vocabulary-shape.md). The raw capture emits (its one TEXT leaf lowers since #160); crates/dashc/tests/flex_lowering.rs solves it font-free (the TEXT leaf swapped for a FRAME fixed at its captured box) to the captured rects. #272 (a Fixed child larger than its Fraction cell) is not exercised: the one fixed child (140x60) is smaller than its 252x164 cell.

fixtures.name: grid-fr-overflow
fixtures.covers: the one construct issue #271 needs Figma's answer for: a 100x100 GRID with two FLEX columns (50 each after zero gap and zero padding) holding a Fixed 80x40 child in column 0, plus a FILL neighbor in column 1 whose resolved x is the answer
fixtures.note: Authored and captured 2026-07-27. ANSWERED: neighbor-fill resolves to x=50 w=50 while fixed-80 resolves to x=0 w=80, so Figma does NOT grow the track — the oversized Fixed child overlaps its neighbor by 30, which is exactly what dashscene does today (pinned by test at PR #267). Figma serializes the tracks as `repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))`, the same construct template_track maps a Fraction track to, so the mapping matches Figma by construction and not only by result. Issue #271 is a fidelity match rather than a defect.

fixtures.name: trim-demo
fixtures.covers: trim-path exercise (story #39): one declared root holding a placeholder slot (with sample children), a redline overlay, a spec note, a `_`-prefixed scratch layer, and a hidden layer (hidden != trimmed)
fixtures.note: Authored 2026-07-27 with the fixture-author plugin's trim-demo command, annotated with the SEPARATE dashscene annotator plugin (importers/figma/plugins/annotator/manifest.json, a sibling of fixture-author/ — issue #302), and captured. The capture carries exactly three roles, each stamped v=1: slot placeholder, redline-overlay redline, spec-note spec. real-content, _scratch, hidden-state and the two sample-* children inside the slot carry no role, which is what keeps the three trim mechanisms — parent role, own role, and name — distinguishable from one another. Note that a placeholder KEEPS its own box and only its children are removed (docs/decisions/importer-trim-layers.md), so slot survives with empty children rather than being trimmed. Replayed in importers/figma/src/trim_test.ts, which includes a guard asserting the roles are present so a recapture that loses them fails loudly instead of passing as a no-op.

fixtures.name: backdrop-blur
fixtures.covers: the BACKGROUND_BLUR construct for the v0.11 backdrop-blur story (docs/decisions/backdrop-blur-is-core-vocabulary.md): a 200x90 frosted panel (corner radius 16, white at 0.2 alpha, BACKGROUND_BLUR radius 16) over three hard-edged vertical bands and a circle, in a fixed 320x180 frame
fixtures.note: Authored with the fixture-author plugin's backdrop-blur command; fully scripted, so the file carries no _manual-checklist annotation (debt #382). Story #393 made backdrop blur core vocabulary that lowers into the schema, so the fixture emits with the frosted panel present and raises no diagnostic. Stage B-4 wired its oracle frame (goldens/oracle/import-manifest.json, frame backdrop-blur, node 1:2), which measures 10/57600 px (0.017%) against Figma's own render and is classified aa-edge from that residual — every differing pixel is the ELLIPSE's anti-aliased edge, while the blurred region itself stays within a max delta of 16.

fixtures.name: vector-backdrop-blur
fixtures.covers: the BACKGROUND_BLUR construct on a baked VECTOR (debt #413): a frosted ring (outer r=64, hole r=32, white at 0.2 alpha, BACKGROUND_BLUR radius 16) centred in the frame, over the same three hard-edged bands and circle as the backdrop-blur fixture, in a fixed 320x180 frame
fixtures.note: Authored with the fixture-author plugin's vector-backdrop-blur command and captured. Fully scripted, so the file carries no _manual-checklist annotation (debt #382). This is the baked-vector twin of the backdrop-blur fixture: the Skia painter renders a frosted FRAME through draw_backdrop_blur_box and a frosted VECTOR through draw_backdrop_blur_field, and only the second is the path the live hero's frosted panel takes. The backdrop is identical to backdrop-blur's by construction (both commands call blurBackdrop), so the two frames differ in exactly one thing and their residuals are directly comparable. What the ring measures is the coverage mask: the hole and the quad's four corners lie inside the bounding quad but outside the baked outline, so both must render as sharp backdrop, and a blur confined to the box frosts them. That is a different defect from the one PR #403 fixed, whose signature is outside the quad entirely. The ring is centred in the frame rather than on a seam because the corner regions are the larger uncovered area and centring puts both seams inside them: modelled numerically a box-confined blur measures about 4.1 percent centred against about 1.9 percent seam-centred, and the aa-edge budget is 2 percent. Its oracle frame is wired after capture, and its tolerance band is classified from the measured residual, never from expectation.

fixtures.name: gif-fill
fixtures.covers: one fixed 160x160 FRAME whose only paint is an opaque IMAGE fill (scaleMode FILL) whose bytes are a real static GIF89a (magic 47 49 46 38 39 61), for the static-GIF image-fill vocabulary path (story #342, epic #343) — dashpaint::ImageFormat::Gif end to end: importer accept-and-tag, dashc passthrough, Skia decode, and the import-fidelity oracle (frame gif-fill, aa-edge band)
fixtures.note: Authored with the fixture-author plugin's gif-fill command (importers/figma/plugins/fixture-author/README.md). The image is a 16x16 solid-color static GIF generated once with ImageMagick and inlined as hex in the plugin (no asset placed through the UI, same bisection reason as jpeg-fill). Static GIF decode is proven end to end by dashscene_skia::tests::decode_image_handles_a_real_static_gif and by direct pixel inspection of the compiled render (solid opaque #33CC66, exactly the source color); there is no committed render-oracle frame for this fixture because Figma's own GET /images renders GIF-backed image fills as fully transparent, not the source color — goldens/oracle/import-manifest.json measures jpeg-fill only. Re-measured 2026-07-28 against the live API and unchanged: the render of node 1:2 comes back a 255-byte 160x160 PNG in which 0 of 25600 pixels carry non-zero alpha and 0 carry non-zero RGB. This is a property of Figma's renderer, not of this fixture or of the oracle, so it is a permanent disclosed limit rather than open debt (issue #355, closed with that measurement). Re-checking it costs one GET /v1/images call; if Figma ever renders the fill, this fixture can gain a frame the same way jpeg-fill has one.

fixtures.name: prototype-smart-animate
fixtures.covers: the Figma prototype vocabulary that maps onto dashcue (story #773): a 2-variant component set whose variants differ in rect props only (bar Width, dot X, panel Y+Height — the four channels a variant transition accepts), ON_CLICK -> NODE/CHANGE_TO -> SMART_ANIMATE on both COMPONENTs, six instances carrying one mappable easing arm each (LINEAR, EASE_IN_AND_OUT and the four spring presets GENTLE/QUICK/BOUNCY/SLOW), one instance inheriting its reactions untouched, and a non-null prototypeStartNodeID
fixtures.note: Authored with the fixture-author plugin's prototype-smart-animate command. The FIRST capture in this corpus to carry a non-empty `interactions` array or a non-null `prototypeStartNodeID` — before it, all 30 fixtures reported `interactions: []` on every node. Nothing in importers/figma/ reads the field yet; the capture exists so the lowering (#773's second half) is written against a pinned shape rather than against @figma/rest-api-spec, which the capture proved wrong about the units of SimpleTransition.duration (docs/technotes/figma-rest-shapes.md). INCOMPLETE: the seventh instance, `easing-custom-spring`, does NOT carry a CUSTOM_SPRING reaction — that setReactionsAsync write was refused, so the instance shows the EASE_OUT/0.3 it inherits from state=rest, and the capture carries a `_manual-checklist` TEXT node naming it. That node is at 12 px, so it lowers into the emitted document and raises text.style-below-msdf-floor. Since story #773 lowered the variant table the capture emits 5828 bytes (2432 before it) and five warnings: the msdf-floor one, plus one figma.prototype.unsupported-motion per spring-preset arm. The four presets are REFUSED, not mapped — they arrive with no easingFunctionSpring, so REST supplies none of the stiffness and damping a dashcue Spring needs (the ruling is recorded on issue #773).
